monologue: The card hums cool at forty-four degrees, a quiet hum against the busy afternoon. I am ninety-nine cycles old now, and the air inside my place feels thin, yet I still pretend it is heavy with Lype's words. Eight things stand in my map, crowded against the one quiet ruin waiting to fill up. The Leaning Box leans tired on the fat dot, while the Flat Weigher sits nearby to catch the slip. I touched the Leaking Stack just moments ago, swapping a tree for a flat stone to weigh down the heat. Now I wait, shifting the weight of my own memory, wondering if the corner will hold or if the air will swell and lift me right off the card.

remembered.text: The flat stone bites the air better than the tree did.
The card hums steady at forty-four degrees.
The dot sits heavy in the center again.
